items.title: Brewers beat Rays to win their first World Series
items.why: The Milwaukee Brewers beat the Tampa Bay Rays 4-1 in Game 5 in St. Petersburg, Florida, on Wednesday night to win the best-of-seven series 4-1. Rookie Cooper Pratt drove in two runs, and Jacob Misiorowski pitched five and two-thirds scoreless innings.
items.changed: Updated: Milwaukee won Game 5 and the series 4-1
items.matters: It is the Brewers' first title since the club began in 1969.

items.title: Samsung's quarterly profit tops 100 trillion won for the first time
items.why: Samsung Electronics made an operating profit of 107.4 trillion won (about $80 billion) in July to September, up more than 780% on a year earlier, driven by demand for AI memory chips. It will pay a 30 trillion won dividend. Its shares fell more than 5% on Thursday morning.
items.matters: The chip division missed some investors' expectations, Bloomberg reports, showing how high hopes for AI profits have become.

items.title: US Federal Reserve holds rates as two officials push for a rise
items.why: The Fed kept its main rate at 3.75% to 4% on Wednesday, by a vote of 10 to 2. Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack wanted another rise. US inflation reached 3.7% in September, driven mainly by energy prices.
items.matters: Chair Kevin Warsh said inflation is too high; traders now expect a rise in December.

items.title: US farmworkers' leader Dolores Huerta dies at 96
items.why: Dolores Huerta, who co-founded the United Farm Workers union with Cesar Chavez in the 1960s, died of cancer on Wednesday, her family says. She coined the slogan 'Sí, se puede' ('Yes, we can') and campaigned for decades for farmworkers, women and civil rights.
items.matters: Her slogan was later taken up by Barack Obama's 2008 campaign; he awarded her the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2012.

items.title: Bank of Canada raises interest rates for the first time since 2023
items.why: Canada's central bank raised its key rate by a quarter point to 2.5% on Wednesday, its first rise since July 2023. Governor Tiff Macklem said it was needed so that high energy prices do not spread through the economy. Inflation was 3.2% in September, Al Jazeera reports.
items.matters: Higher rates mean dearer mortgages and loans; the bank says it may need to raise them again.

items.title: Up to 50,000 people flee clashes in southern Ethiopia into Kenya
items.why: Fighting between the regional forces of Ethiopia's Somali and Oromia regions around the border town of Moyale began on 20 October. The UN refugee agency says up to 50,000 people have crossed into Kenya, citing local authorities. Several people have died, sources told AFP.
items.matters: Many are sheltering in schools and churches in Kenya's Moyale County; UNHCR says numbers are still rising.

items.title: Putin hosts African leaders at Russia-Africa summit in Moscow
items.why: Delegations from 48 African countries, 22 led by their heads of state, are at the third Russia-Africa summit in Moscow this week. President Vladimir Putin said Russia does not practise 'neo-colonial exploitation' and offered grain, fertiliser and help with infrastructure. He accused Western countries of trapping African nations in debt.
items.matters: Russia is competing with Western countries and China for trade and influence in Africa; a final declaration is expected.

items.title: At least 68 killed as two high-speed trains collide in central Spain
items.why: A Renfe high-speed train hit a stationary Iryo train near Urda, in Toledo province, on Wednesday morning. Castilla-La Mancha's regional government says at least 68 people died. Transport Minister Óscar Puente says a safety system had failed and calls a control-centre order to let the train resume 'inexplicable'.
items.matters: Spain is holding three days of national mourning; trains between Madrid and Andalusia are suspended.
items.changed: Updated: the death toll rose to at least 68; a control-centre order is being investigated
Updated: Iran says it is reviewing ideas with mediators; Reuters reports a new Qatari draft, which an Iranian official denies
items.title: Iran says it is still talking to mediators about reopening Hormuz
items.why: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi says Tehran is in close contact with mediators on its 'seven-day plan', a ceasefire followed by a phased reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. Reuters reported that Qatar handed Iran a new draft deal; a senior Iranian official denied a new proposal was made.
items.matters: Saudi, Turkish and Pakistani officials held talks in Tehran on Monday; President Trump has rejected the seven-day plan, CBS reports.

items.title: South Korea fines Google and Apple over app store payment rules
items.why: South Korea's media regulator, the KMCC, fined Google 42.9 billion won and Apple 20.8 billion won (about $47.6 million together) on Wednesday. It says they pushed developers to use their own payment systems and delayed app reviews without clear reasons. Both must allow links to outside payment sites.
items.matters: It is the first penalty under Korea's 2021 law against forcing app makers to use one payment system. Apple says it disagrees.

items.title: Lancet report links nearly 3 million deaths to climate-driven heat
items.why: The tenth Lancet Countdown report, by 146 researchers from 30 countries, says heat was linked to more than 540,000 deaths a year from 2016 to 2023, about 68% of them due to climate change. An estimated 710,000 heat deaths in 2023 set a record.
items.matters: The authors call for climate change to be declared a global health emergency ahead of next month's COP31 summit in Türkiye.

items.title: SK Hynix’s quarterly revenue passes 100 trillion won for the first time
items.why: South Korean memory-chip maker SK Hynix reported third-quarter revenue of 104.6 trillion won, up 328% on a year earlier, and operating profit of 83.3 trillion won. It plans to return about 100 trillion won to shareholders this year.
items.matters: Seoul's Kospi index jumped 6.63% to 6,012 on Wednesday as SK Hynix shares rose almost 11% and Samsung's 9%.
items.changed: Updated: Seoul's Kospi index jumped 6.6% on the results

items.title: Fourth-tier Fleetwood knock Arsenal out of the League Cup on penalties
items.why: Fleetwood Town, 18th in England's League Two, drew 1-1 with Premier League champions Arsenal at their Highbury Stadium on Tuesday, then won the shoot-out 5-3. Arsenal's 16-year-old Max Dowman was sent off late in the game.
items.matters: Fleetwood reach the quarter-finals; several outlets rank it among the biggest upsets in the competition’s history.

items.changed: Updated: he has landed in Miami and says he is Brazil's rightful leader
items.title: Flávio Bolsonaro lands in Miami after leaving Brazil despite court order
items.why: Brazil's defeated presidential candidate landed in Miami on Wednesday with his family, after travelling through Argentina and Ecuador despite a Supreme Court order to hand over his passports in a money-laundering inquiry, which he denies. The US granted the family visas. In a letter, he called himself Brazil's rightful leader.
items.matters: Brazil's electoral court, international observers and his own party have recognised President Lula's re-election.

items.title: Abhishek Sharma's 35-ball hundred seals India's T20 series win in New Zealand
items.why: Abhishek Sharma hit 113 off 38 balls as India chased 199 in 13.2 overs to beat New Zealand by six wickets in Wellington on 27 October. The win gives India an unbeatable 3-0 lead in the five-match series.
items.matters: India's 118 runs in the first six overs was a record for men's T20 internationals, BBC Sport says.

items.title: Finnish and Norwegian leaders hold rare phone call with Putin
items.why: Finland's President Alexander Stubb and Norway's Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre spoke with Vladimir Putin from Helsinki on Tuesday for about an hour and a half, they say. Their offices said the aim was to pass on messages before US-mediated Ukraine–Russia talks in Abu Dhabi in early November.
items.matters: Most Western European leaders have avoided direct contact with Putin since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

items.title: Greenhouse gases reached record levels in 2025, UN weather agency says
items.why: Carbon dioxide in the atmosphere averaged a record 426.8 parts per million in 2025, 53% above pre-industrial levels, the World Meteorological Organization said on 27 October. Methane and nitrous oxide also hit records. The rise was smaller than 2024's jump but above the decade's average.
items.matters: The figures will feed into the COP31 climate talks in Antalya, Turkey, from 9 to 20 November.

items.title: Drone strike on market in Sudan's Nyala kills dozens
items.why: A drone strike hit a market in Nyala, in South Darfur, on Monday evening. Doctors Without Borders says the hospital it supports received 36 bodies and over 150 wounded; the rights group Emergency Lawyers says more than 100 died and blames the army, which has not commented.
items.matters: Nyala is the main base of the paramilitary RSF, at war with Sudan's army since April 2023.

items.title: Australian jumping spiders show two sleep stages, including REM-like sleep
items.why: Researchers at Germany's University of Bonn filmed the fringed jumping spider, found in northern Australia, at night and found a quiet sleep stage and a REM-like stage with eye movements and twitching. After disturbed nights the spiders spent nearly 80% more time in REM-like sleep. The study is in PNAS.
items.matters: An Australian expert called it the most complete behavioural case for sleep in any arachnid, though brain activity was not measured.

items.title: Mbappé apologises after Chinese brands drop him over Mao joke
items.why: Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappé called his comment "ill-judged" after a video showed him describing Mao Zedong as a Chinese dictator while discussing a meme. Drinks maker Dongpeng, dairy firm Mengniu and cheese maker Milkground ended their deals with him.
items.matters: China Media Group suspended broadcasts of his La Liga matches, France 24 reports; La Liga also apologised.

items.title: South Korean chip shares jump after Anthropic's stock market filing
items.why: South Korea's Kospi share index closed 3.09% higher at 5,638 on Tuesday, its first gain in four sessions. Samsung Electronics rose 4.23% and SK hynix 5.18%, after Anthropic's filing for a US listing revived hopes for demand for AI memory chips.
items.matters: Trading in program buy orders in Seoul was paused for five minutes as prices rose quickly, the Herald Business reports.

items.title: Fire sweeps through Seoul’s last shantytown, displacing over 100 people
items.why: A fire that began on Tuesday afternoon in Guryong Village, beside Seoul’s wealthy Gangnam district in South Korea, took about 13 hours to put out. Officials say 107 residents from 77 households were displaced and one woman was slightly hurt.
items.matters: Strong winds and a shortage of water hampered firefighters; police and fire officials are investigating the cause.

items.changed: Updated: with nearly 90% counted the deadlock holds; final results are due on 4 November
items.title: Israel's election ends in deadlock, with neither bloc reaching a majority
items.why: With nearly 90% of votes counted, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc is on course for 53 of the Knesset's 120 seats and Gadi Eisenkot's opposition bloc for 48, Al Jazeera reports; 61 are needed. Over 500,000 special ballots are still being counted.
items.matters: Official results are due on 4 November; President Herzog then has a week to choose who tries to form a government.

items.title: HSBC profit rises 32% but its shares fall in Hong Kong
items.why: HSBC reported pre-tax profit of $9.6bn for July to September on Tuesday, up 32% on a year earlier, and announced another share buyback of up to $1bn. Revenue from its wealth business was flat, Reuters reports, and the bank's shares fell between 5% and 7% in Hong Kong.
items.matters: Profit was slightly below what analysts expected, and slowing growth in wealth management worried investors, Reuters and TT report.

items.title: Local ceasefire begins in Russian-held Oleshky so aid can reach civilians
items.why: A ceasefire around the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky, in Ukraine's Kherson region, began early on Tuesday, both sides' militaries say. The White House says Melania Trump brokered it so aid can arrive and civilians can leave; Ukrainian officials estimate about 2,000 people remain.
items.matters: Neither side has said how long it will last; the Kremlin says it could be a model for similar arrangements.

items.changed: Updated: the cyclone made landfall early on 28 October and is weakening
items.title: Cyclone Arnab makes landfall in India's Andhra Pradesh, then weakens
items.why: Cyclone Arnab crossed the coast near Yanam, about 20 km from Narsapur, early on Wednesday with gusts of up to 150 km/h, India's weather office says. It has weakened to a severe cyclonic storm. Officials quoted by the PTI news agency say two people died after touching live wires.
items.matters: Odisha says about 100,000 people were moved to safety; heavy rain is forecast inland in Odisha and Jharkhand.

items.changed: Updated: Jordan strikes Syria; Syria says civilians were killed
items.title: Jordan strikes southern Syria after deadly Karak church attack
items.why: Jordan's military says its jets hit armed groups' hideouts in southern Syria on Monday, after Friday's attack on a funeral at a church in Karak killed nine people. Syria's civil defence says seven civilians died, including three children, and Damascus says it was not consulted.
items.matters: Jordan arrested three suspects in the church attack on Monday; Syria has closed its main border crossing with Jordan.

items.title: Serbia's Vučić concedes election defeat to student-led movement
items.why: Aleksandar Vučić conceded on Sunday night that his Serbian Progressive Party had lost the snap parliamentary election to the Student List, which grew out of two years of anti-corruption protests. Vučić said early results gave the students 135 to 140 of 250 seats. Turnout was close to 70%.
items.matters: Final official results are still to come, election officials say.

items.changed: Updated: police now say at least 58 died
items.title: Police say 58 killed in gunmen's attack on Nigerian village
items.why: Armed men attacked Binnari village in Nigeria's Taraba State during its market day on Friday. Taraba police say at least 58 people died, including 15 who drowned when a canoe capsized as they fled. Police had first confirmed 10 deaths.

items.changed: Updated: confirmed cases pass 10,000, Congo's health ministry says
items.title: DR Congo's Ebola cases pass 10,000 as outbreak keeps spreading
items.why: DR Congo's health ministry says confirmed Ebola cases have reached 10,060, with 4,887 deaths, across 66 health zones in eight provinces. About 80% of new cases come from outside known contact chains, AP reports. Uganda now requires citizens returning from Congo to quarantine for 21 days.
items.matters: It is the second-largest Ebola outbreak on record, and no vaccine or treatment is approved for this Bundibugyo strain.

items.changed: Updated: Sri Lanka beat Pakistan to reach the final and knock England out
items.title: Pakistan to meet Sri Lanka in tri-series final as England go out
items.why: Pakistan, who beat England by one wicket on 25 October thanks to Shadab Khan's unbeaten 113, will play Sri Lanka in the final on 31 October. Sri Lanka bowled Pakistan out for 110 in Lahore on 27 October and won by eight wickets, ending England's hopes.
items.matters: Dilshan Madushanka took a career-best five for 34; England have lost all three of their matches in the series.

items.changed: Updated: 11 deaths in a day, the year's highest; toll reaches 400
items.title: Bangladesh's dengue death toll this year reaches 400
items.why: Bangladesh's health directorate reported 11 dengue deaths in the 24 hours to 8am on 27 October, the highest daily toll this year, and 2,071 hospital admissions. This year's toll is 400 deaths, 155 of them in October, with 128,237 people admitted to hospital.
items.matters: Dengue usually peaks in Bangladesh's June–September monsoon, but this year cases are still rising in late October.
